Package com.nexuslink.protocol.db

Class JdbcConnectionPool

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.db.JdbcConnectionPool
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class JdbcConnectionPool extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Owns one HikariDataSource per connection profile and hands out pooled connections. A "profile" here is identified by a caller-supplied key (see keyFor(String, String)), so two SQL tabs pointed at the same URL/user share a single pool while different targets stay isolated.

Why this works with on-demand drivers

The tricky part of pooling on top of the JdbcDriverRegistry/DriverShim strategy is that a driver loaded from a downloaded jar lives in a child classloader that HikariCP can't see. We sidestep it by never setting driverClassName on the HikariConfig: with only a JDBC URL set, Hikari's internal data source resolves the driver through DriverManager.getDriver(String), which finds the DriverShim that ExternalDriverLoader registered against the app classloader. Bundled drivers auto-register the same way via the JDBC ServiceLoader SPI. So the pooled path and the direct DriverManager path resolve drivers identically.

The manager is thread-safe and AutoCloseable: close() shuts every pool down.

  • Method Details

    • keyFor

      public static String keyFor(String url, String user)
      A stable key for a connection profile. Keying on URL + user keeps pools separate per target and per identity, without ever holding on to the password.

    • dataSourceFor

      public com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariDataSource dataSourceFor(String key, String url, String user, String password, Map<String,String> extraProps, JdbcPoolConfig config)
      Returns the pool for key, creating it on first use from the given profile. Subsequent calls with the same key return the existing pool and ignore the (assumed identical) profile — matching Hikari's "one data source per profile" model.
